settings.settingsAgentNotifyNote: Only controls notifications initiated by agents. Completion, deployment, and other notifications are unaffected.
settings.settingsCodexAutoNameHint: For each unnamed session, your chosen assistant runs one small turn using the session's request and latest reply. This uses that assistant's quota and never replaces a name you chose.
settings.settingsCodexDefaultEffortHint: Used for a new Codex session without its own effort choice. A child agent may still choose its own effort.
settings.settingsCompactWindowHint: Only for Claude sessions Clawdline opens — children, Root Assignments, handoffs — never Codex, never a session you opened. Past this many tokens of context the session replaces its history with a summary: every later call re-reads fewer tokens, which is where most of a long session's cost goes, but the summary can lose detail, files get read again, and each compaction takes about ten seconds. Empty leaves Claude Code alone; it then compacts near its own 1M window. A task can ask for its own. Takes effect at the next launch.
settings.settingsCompactWindowInvalid: A whole number of tokens from {min} to {max}, or empty for none.
settings.settingsDefaultModelHint: Used only when Clawdline opens a new session without another model choice. A child agent or one session may still choose its own model.
settings.settingsFollow: Show the selected session in the terminal
settings.settingsFollowHint: This selects that session's tab without bringing the terminal to the front. Otherwise, every press of Tab would move the keyboard away from the field you are typing in.
settings.settingsHooksHint: Once installed, Claude Code signals when a turn starts, ends, or needs your answer, without waiting for Clawdline to check again. The screen still determines each state; this only controls how quickly Clawdline checks it.
settings.settingsHooksLegacy: This file still has the older hook (clawdline/hook.sh). Claude Code runs it every turn, but this version does not read the note it leaves. Nothing breaks; it only runs an extra small command each time. To remove it, delete the entry containing clawdline/hook.sh from this file, or choose “Remove” in the older app's settings (which removes only its own entry).
settings.settingsHooksNone: This version does not install a hook. It reads session state from Claude Code's own state files.
settings.settingsHooksOff: Not installed — all states read from the screen
settings.settingsHooksOn: Installed — no session has reported yet
settings.settingsHooksStray: This file contains a clawdline-next/hook.sh entry, but this version does not read it.
settings.settingsHooksWhat: A hook is a command Claude Code runs at specific moments, registered in ~/.claude/settings.json. The older Clawdline hook leaves a note when a turn starts or ends, a permission dialog appears, or Claude Code asks a question. The older app then reads that session's screen right away. Without the hook, it checks every 20 seconds while the input box is hidden, so a permission request may take 20 seconds to appear in the menu bar. With the hook, it takes less than a second.
settings.settingsHooksWhy: Installing a hook changes Claude Code's settings file so it runs an extra command at eight points in every turn. This version cannot yet read those notes, so installation would only run unused commands. It does not offer installation or change ~/.claude/settings.json. The install button will appear once reading the notes is supported.
settings.settingsHooksWhyHead: Why is it absent from this version?
settings.settingsHooksWithout: Claude Code writes each session's state (busy, idle, waiting) to ~/.claude/sessions/. This version reads those files about every two seconds. The session list states, menu bar count, notch animation, and options shown when an answer is needed all come from there; no hook is needed. Compared with the older app's hook, a change may appear up to about two seconds later instead of within one second. Sessions without readable state files, such as Codex, are read from the terminal screen.
settings.settingsHotkeyHint: The default is ⌥Space. If another app (such as Alfred) uses the same combination, both may respond and Clawdline cannot detect that; choose another combination, or narrow “Where it works” below to terminals only.
settings.settingsHotkeyLegacy: The older Clawdline is also running and uses {combo}, so one press opens two input boxes. Quit the older app. If it starts at login, turn off “Launch at Login” in its menu.

settings.settingsHotkeySystem: {combo} is reserved by the operating system, so it was not registered. The ✳ in Clawdline's menu still opens the input box; press the button above to choose another combination.
settings.settingsHotkeyUnreadable: The hotkey “{spec}” in the settings file could not be read, so it was not registered. The ✳ in the menu bar can still open the input box; use the button above to record a new shortcut.
settings.settingsNotchHint: Put a character by the camera. Turning this off draws nothing and does not create a window.
settings.settingsOrchestratorClose: After a child session reports back
settings.settingsOrchestratorCloseHint: Close its tab after it reports. Leave a timed-out tab open so you can inspect what happened.
settings.settingsOrchestratorEnabled: Let one session dispatch work to another
settings.settingsOrchestratorEnabledHint: A session with the clawdline skill can open a new tab, type instructions into it, then report back when it finishes. When this is off, new dispatches are blocked; tasks already running continue.
settings.settingsOrchestratorMaxHint: The default is five. The limit is per session, not per machine. Each child is a terminal tab with an assistant doing work in it.
settings.settingsOrchestratorNotify: Report back to the dispatching session
settings.settingsOrchestratorNotifyHint: When the task ends, type a line into that session.
settings.settingsOrchestratorPermission: How far a child can proceed on its own
settings.settingsOrchestratorPermissionH: Nobody watches a child's tab. A session that pauses for approval will remain there until it times out. Since a dispatched task runs commands and writes files, any setting short of the last one can stop it. A task may require stricter permission, but cannot exceed this setting.
settings.settingsPushDelivery: Notify me when a session reports delivery
settings.settingsPushDeliveryHint: Notify once per report; repeated reports of the same delivery stay quiet.
settings.settingsPushFanout: Notify me when a batch of dispatched tasks finishes
settings.settingsPushFanoutHint: Notify once for the whole batch, including the number of failures.
settings.settingsRemoteHint: When this is off, nothing outside this machine can reach it. When it is on, the session list is available on 127.0.0.1 — to a browser here, a phone connected through a tunnel, or a script. What it exposes is repository names, branches, and work titles, so it stays off until you turn it on.
settings.settingsRemoteServe: Let a browser or your phone view your sessions
settings.settingsRemoteWriteHint: Every signed-in device paired with this machine can send. Clawdline Cloud commands can still be turned off for this machine with clawdline cloud commands off.
settings.settingsReopen: Show and hide the input bar with the terminal
settings.settingsReopenHint: The input bar hides when you switch away from the terminal and returns when you switch back. Press Esc when you are done with it for now.
settings.settingsScopeHint: Leave this list empty to use the shortcut everywhere. Removing the last app turns on the switch above; turn it off to bring the list back. The settings file stores bundle IDs, and a manually edited list works too.
settings.settingsSessionTerminalHint: A different question from where the hotkey works, above. Automatic uses iTerm2 while it is open and tmux while it is not. Choosing iTerm2 names iTerm2: when it is closed the start is refused, even with a tmux server running. With tmux installed, both open the session in its own tmux session and show it in an iTerm2 tab, so reading and typing never wait on iTerm2. iTerm2 (native tab) runs the session in the tab itself, as before. tmux always opens in a tmux server, even with iTerm2 open. The next session follows this; nothing needs restarting.
settings.settingsSmartNotificationsHint: Use Haiku to explain what just finished. If generation fails, send the original notification.
settings.settingsStateHookHint: Whenever a session starts, finishes, or asks you something, Clawdline runs your program and passes the details through environment variables. This belongs in the settings file because it is an argv array, not a command line; a path with spaces remains one path.

settings.settingsTunnelHint: cloudflared connects outward from this machine — no port forwarding, and nothing listens on your network. It starts only after a device has been paired, because behind the tunnel are every repository name and work title on this machine.
settings.settingsVoiceLanguageHint: Whisper processes voice on this machine, no matter which browser or phone sent the recording. “Follow Clawdline” checks the language on the General tab first.
